description:
Surfaced 2026-05-08 by PRINCIPAL after Engagement B substrate ship + manual deploy to ariadne-core-workspace. Today's deploy required POLYBIUS to (a) realize the substrate had updated, (b) manually run install.sh --dry-run, (c) verify drift, (d) deploy. That sequence is fine for occasional updates but doesn't scale as the substrate matures or as consumer workspaces multiply.

## Problem

- the-stoa is canonical substrate source for MAJOR_PLINY.md, MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md, operating-disciplines.md, 10 CAPTAIN envelopes, templates, skills.
- Consumer workspaces (ariadne-core-workspace, possibly agent-team-on-beadwork, agent-gauntlet, others) deploy via substrate/install.sh.
- After deploy, if the-stoa is updated, consumer workspaces silently drift.
- Current detection: manually `cd substrate && ./install.sh --target project --project-dir <ws> --dry-run` per workspace, eyeball output. Doesn't scale; easy to forget; no aggregation across workspaces.

## Proposed feature: skill that checks all consumer workspaces for drift

New skill at `substrate/skills/check-substrate-updates/`. Invokable via Skill tool or via a one-liner from any agent (POLYBIUS, PLINY, pair-programmer Major).

Behavior:
1. Read a workspace registry (substrate/consumer-workspaces.txt or auto-discovered via filesystem walk under ~/claude_projects/).
2. For each registered workspace: invoke install.sh --dry-run, capture which files would change.
3. Aggregate output:

   ```
   ariadne-core-workspace            STALE (4 files; last deploy 2026-05-04)
     - operating-disciplines.md       +156 lines
     - MAJOR_PLINY.md                  +86 lines
     - MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md               +2 lines
     - templates/paste-instruction-template.md  +2 lines
   agent-team-on-beadwork            CURRENT
   agent-gauntlet                    NOT-STOA-DEPLOYED (no .claude/operating-disciplines.md)
   ```

4. Optional flag --since to show substrate-side commits between last deploy and current: `git log --oneline <last-deploy-sha>..HEAD substrate/`. Helps PRINCIPAL decide whether the drift is worth deploying now or can wait.

5. Optional flag --deploy to apply install.sh against any STALE workspace identified (with confirmation prompt or --yes).

## Implementation shape

- substrate/skills/check-substrate-updates/SKILL.md — skill metadata + frontmatter + trigger description
- substrate/skills/check-substrate-updates/check.sh — bash implementation; reuses install.sh --dry-run as the drift primitive
- substrate/consumer-workspaces.txt — explicit registry (one path per line); alternative is auto-discovery but explicit registry is more deterministic

Workspace registry seed (current consumers I'm aware of):
- /c/Users/denso/claude_projects/ariadne-core-workspace
- (others TBD per PRINCIPAL's actual workspace inventory — survey at implementation time)

## Out of scope

- Activation-time auto-check in MAJOR_PLINY / MAJOR_POLYBIUS (more intrusive; could be a v2 follow-up if drift becomes painful)
- Auto-deploy without operator confirmation (security: substrate canon edits SHOULD be ratified by a human before propagating to consumer workspaces, especially since they affect agent role-files)
- Cross-machine substrate sync (the-stoa is per-machine; multi-machine canon is a separate concern)

## Gauntlet

ADA + CATO eyeball. New skill + small bash script + plain-text registry file. ~150-300 LOC total. No DAEDALUS / ARGUS / VERA / ZENO unless something substantive surfaces during build.

## Sequencing

P3. Not blocking; today's manual deploy was tractable. But useful soon — multi-workspace deploy reality is real now (post Engagement B), and the friction will compound as the substrate evolves. Bundle into next stoa substrate dispatch or ship standalone when convenient.

## Empirical anchor

2026-05-08 PRINCIPAL surface during Engagement B post-ship deploy. POLYBIUS manually ran install.sh --dry-run + install.sh against ariadne-core-workspace; no aggregated visibility across multiple workspaces; PRINCIPAL flagged the gap and asked for a check skill.
title: Substrate-update check skill — detect drift between the-stoa canon and consumer workspaces
